author: DTrim99
body:
Agreed. PE and Taxsim match here — Delaware's earned income credit is **20% of the $2,306 federal EIC = $461.18**, computed once for the return (Schedule PIT-RSS), which nets to siitax $245.13. TaxAct's lower result comes from computing a separate DE EIC for each spouse's column under combined-separate filing, exactly the piece you flagged. Delaware's EIC is a single 20%-of-federal credit, so PE and Taxsim's one-credit treatment is the straightforward reading, and I'm happy to leave the per-spouse-EIC difference alone as you suggest.

If you ever want me to check whether Delaware actually intends a per-column EIC split on combined-separate returns (the way it does split the tax), just say the word — but I'll treat this as resolved for now.
